competitive_landscape: The corridor is served today by conventional fast-craft ferry operators whose volumes are surging — over 1.1 million sea passengers and a 93% year-on-year jump are unambiguous demand proof. The status quo is a fixed-schedule, weather-exposed diesel service with demand outpacing capacity; a fast, quiet, reliable foiling layer is the natural upgrade. No foiling operator runs here.

regulatory_note: Greek flag / EU; Hellenic Coast Guard certification and Greek cabotage rules favour EU-flagged vessels. The cross-water crossing runs through established CIQ ferry terminals on both coasts and is best approached as a controlled, scheduled pilot in coordination with the relevant port and maritime authorities. EU maritime-decarbonisation policy adds a clean-fleet tailwind.
seasonality: Peak summer (Jun–Sep) carries the heaviest traffic; the etesian (meltemi) NW wind builds afternoon chop that roughens the conventional fast craft. Foiling flight above the surface keeps the short crossing smooth and the schedule reliable, extending the workable window at the shoulders.

summary: Chios sits barely five nautical miles off Çeşme on the Turkish coast — the shortest international water hop in the region and a corridor where ferry demand is already booming. Over 1.1 million passengers crossed from Türkiye to nearby Greek islands by sea in a single year, a 93% jump, on more than 8,600 sailings. This is proven short-water demand, not a speculative luxury circuit: a fast, quiet, reliable foiling crossing modernises a habit travellers have already adopted, with the intra-North-Aegean hops to Samos and Lesvos all inside all-electric range.
tagline: The shortest cross-water hop in the Aegean — a proven, fast-growing short-water market minutes off the Turkish coast.
